sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Excess Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors and Resistors

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law with Anglo-American commercial and maritime law influence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 2012)
Panama-Netherlands Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement
Panama-Germany Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT Framework), Executive Decree 148 of 2013 (Beneficial Ownership Registry), Law 41 of 2007, Unified Criminal Code (Articles 254-256), and UAF Resolutions implementing FATF recommendations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or national civil registry of UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization at a Panamanian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified bank reference letter and current KYC profile of shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution under the regulation of the Panamanian Superintendent of Banks or equivalent home regulator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with notarization of the signature if origin is non-Hague

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association (Pacto Social) of any existing parent corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá or foreign companies registry of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if home state is a Hague member) or Consular Legalization at the nearest Panamanian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and proof of no dissolution proceedings of existing corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corresponding Company Registry or Tax Authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and counterparties against the Panamanian Office of the Superintendent of Banks sanctions list, the UAF's PEP registry, OFAC SDN/Consolidated List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated sanctions list, and local Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) lists, supplemented by adverse media and negative news checks. All screening must be documented and retained for at least five years following termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Portal de Consulta y Reserva de Razones Sociales (online services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed company names must be in Spanish or transliterated into Latin/Spanish characters. The suffix 'S.A.' (Sociedad Anónima) is mandatory. Names must avoid exact or phonetically identical coincidence with existing registered names and must not be misleadingly similar to Panamanian government entities or international organizations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant (through a licensed attorney or registered agent) may file a 'Recurso de Revocatoria' with the Registro Público de Panamá within 5 business days of the rejection notice. The registry will re-examine the proposed name for compliance and uniqueness. Alternatively, a new name request may be filed online without prejudice. In exceptional cases, judicial review may be sought in the Jurisdicción Contencioso-Administrativa of the Supreme Court of Panama.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in Panama is legally required, but may consist of the office of a licensed registered agent. Virtual/remote management is permissible for passive electronic inventory distribution without local physical stock, provided the company maintains its registered agent, a resident fiscal representative, and full documentary substance files (board resolutions, records, and accounting books).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% annual probability for a low-risk passive components distributor in Panama; this may rise to 30% if there are UBO irregularities, failure to maintain registered office documentation, or adverse AML/KYC triggers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas), as amended, particularly Articles 1-12 on formation, Articles 13-19 on capital stock, Articles 20-36 on shareholders and directors, and Articles 37-63 on corporate books and reporting; subsidiary registry regulations issued by the Dirección General de Registro Público.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Departamento de Personas Jurídicas
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Sociedad Anónima. The articles may declare a nominal authorized capital (customarily US$10,000 divided into 100 shares) but no escrow account, deposit, or full payment is required at incorporation. Shares may be issued for consideration deemed sufficient by the board, subject to general creditor-protection rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF PA_CORP S.A. — At a duly convened meeting, the board unanimously: (1) approves the public deed of incorporation subscribed on [DATE] and the articles of association as adopted; (2) accepts the subscription of 10,000 common voting shares, declared fully paid as credited in the capital ledger; (3) designates the registered office of the company in the Republic of Panama as [REGISTERED ADDRESS] and confirms the resident agent; (4) appoints [PRESIDENT], [SECRETARY], and [TREASURER] as officers with full statutory authority; and (5) authorizes the president and secretary, jointly or severally, to execute tax, regulatory, banking, and municipal filings, to establish commercial and operational licenses, and to open bank accounts necessary to commence passive electronic components distribution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Personas Jurídicas, via the electronic services portal of the Registro Público
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternate corporate names in Spanish through a licensed Panamanian attorney or the online portal. The Registry verifies that the proposed names are not identical or confusingly similar to existing legal entities. Upon approval, obtain the Certificado de Registro de Nombre, which is valid for 30 days, and pay the applicable name-search and stamp taxes.
required_dossiers: Completed corporate name search application
Copy of identification documents (cédula or passport) for proposed shareholders and directors
Payment receipt for name search and municipal stamp tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, file a new name application or submit a written notarized consent/disclaimer from the prior user. An appeal may be filed with the Dirección General del Registro Público within two business days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública of the Republic of Panama, in coordination with the licensed Panamanian attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The attorney prepares the Spanish-language escritura constitutiva containing the corporate name, domicile, specific object, duration, authorized capital, share classes, board provisions, resident-agent acceptance, and optional special clauses permitted by Law 32 of 1927. The incorporators or their authorized attorney-in-fact appear before a Panamanian notary, verify identity, and execute the deed; notarial seals and fees are affixed.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Registro de Nombre
Passport or cédula of all incorporators and initial directors
Final draft of the articles of incorporation
Written acceptance of the resident agent and registered office
Evidence of payment of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses due to Spanish-language defects or identification discrepancies, correct the translation or documentation and resubmit. If an incorporator is unavailable, execute through a properly authenticated special power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Inscription and Corporate Folio Creation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Departamento de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized public deed and attachments for inscription. The Registry verifies the corporate name, permitted object, capital clauses, and resident agent acceptance, assigns a Folio Electrónico (Ficha de Persona Jurídica), stamps the deed, and returns a certified copy. After inscription, the company's stock and corporate-book protocolization, known as rúbrica, is completed separately.
required_dossiers: Original and copy of the notarized public deed of incorporation
Certificado de Registro de Nombre
Resident agent acceptance and registered-office designation
Receipt of the registration fee computed on authorized capital
Proof of payment of stamp taxes on fiscal paper
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Defectos notice, the applicant has the statutory cure period to correct the noted defects by brief or amended deed. If rejection is confirmed, lodge a reconsideration request with the Director-General of the Public Registry before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, regional office for Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, file the tax-registration application to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC). Provide the company's tax domicile, legal representative details, and the ISIC 4652 classification for wholesale distribution of electronic components. Upon approval, obtain the RUC certificate and register for electronic invoicing in the DGI portal.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered public deed
Ficha de persona jurídica or corporate certificate from the Registry
Identification documents for the legal representative
Proof of tax domicile (lease or utility invoice)
Completed DGI RUC registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC is blocked for discrepancies between the deed and application, file a rectified deed or submit a DGI amendment form to align the corporate name, domicile, or economic activity code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá, Tesorería Municipal, Sección de Aviso de Operación; other municipalities as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Aviso de Operación application describing passive electronic components distribution and warehousing. The municipality assesses the annual operating tax based on estimated gross revenue and premises size, conducts a simple site inspection where required, and issues the municipal operating permit. The permit must be renewed annually.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and taxpayer data sheet
Certified copy of the public deed and corporate ficha
Lease agreement or ownership title for the operating premises
Municipal inspection form and simple floor plan
Identification of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If denied for zoning issues, obtain a Certificado de Uso de Suelo from the relevant municipal office and reapply. If the company activity is misclassified, amend the aviso and pay any corrected fee; an appeal may be presented to the Mayor within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá and Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil (SINAPROC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the warehouse floor plan and fire-prevention layout for the storage of multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors. Install extinguishers, emergency exits, and evacuation signage, then schedule and pass the fire-safety inspection. Upon approval, obtain the Certificado de Seguridad y Prevención contra Incendios and comply with SINAPROC's workplace evacuation-plan requirements.
required_dossiers: Municipal Aviso de Operación or lease evidence
Warehouse floor plan showing storage aisles, exits, and extinguishers
Fire-extinguisher installation certificates
Electrical installation review, if requested
Identification of the responsible safety officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection identifies code violations, complete the remedial actions within the mandated period, provide photographic or certificate evidence, and request re-inspection. Administrative appeals may be filed before the Fire Department evaluation committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Normas y Evaluación Ambiental
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the passive electronic-components distribution and warehouse operation is exempt or falls under Category I (low environmental complexity). For a non-manufacturing warehouse with no hazardous processes, submit the applicable environmental registration or initial environmental report, including a simple waste-management plan for packaging and rejected or obsolete electronic components. If MiAMBIENTE requires a full EIA, engage a registered consultant to prepare the corresponding study.
required_dossiers: EIA category-determination application form
Project description and warehouse floor size
RUC certificate and municipal Aviso de Operación
Waste storage and disposal plan
Declaration that no chemical processing or solvent use occurs on site
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MiAMBIENTE assigns a higher classification, submit supplemental studies or an Informe Ambiental de Categoría I, pay the applicable evaluation fee, or file an administrative reconsideration within ten business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección de Comercio Interior, for commercial wholesale activity; Municipio de Panamá for the municipal Aviso de Operación; MiAMBIENTE for environmental clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Operating Notice), complemented by Certificado de Seguridad y Prevención contra Incendios and applicable MiAMBIENTE environmental registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Normas y Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Baja Complejidad Ambiental) — environmental registration or an initial environmental report is required only when storage area or waste generation exceeds thresholds; pure passive electronic inventory distribution without manufacturing is generally exempt from a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are expected from warehousing and distribution. The operation must comply with Panamanian national effluent limits for sanitary discharges to municipal sewers, solid-waste handling rules, prohibitions on uncontrolled disposal of electronic components, and ambient air quality standards for any incidental generator or HVAC emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, structural and load verification for the warehouse floor by the municipal engineering office, workplace evacuation plan approved by SINAPROC, employer registration with the Caja de Seguro Social, and workplace health-and-safety registration with MITRADEL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama; e-portal: Sede Electrónica T@S (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Panamanian Sociedad Anónima, a licensed resident agent files DGI Form RUC via Sede Electrónica, attaching certified copy of Public Registry entry, articles of incorporation, ID of directors/legal representative, and proof of fiscal address. The DGI then assigns the RUC/NIT and issues an ITBMS account. For a foreign entity without Panamanian establishment, registration is required only upon deriving Panama-source income or completing taxable transactions; a legal representative must be appointed and a local address maintained.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or similar election exists; all S.A.s are subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Optional elections include group consolidation with prior DGI authorization, the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime, and small-taxpayer fixed-amount regimes for entities below turnover thresholds.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios, a VAT equivalent)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold: all persons performing taxable supplies in Panama must register as ITBMS taxpayers from the first supply; the small-taxpayer simplified regime applies to qualifying operations with annual gross receipts up to B/.36,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic issuance through DGI-approved billing systems (Facturación Electrónica). Invoices are transmitted in XML/JSON via API to the Sede Electrónica, validated in real time, and assigned a fiscal authorization number. Digital stamping and periodic clearance reporting (RIT, IRE) apply to active ITBMS taxpayers. From 2024, large and medium taxpayers cannot use non-electronic invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Sales of tangible goods qualify for ITBMS 0% when ownership is transferred to a non-Panamanian resident and goods are exported to a third country from Panama, evidenced by customs exit. Offshore services for non-resident use outside Panama also qualify. The distributor of passive electronic components may zero-rate FOB/CIF/FCA export transactions to foreign distributors/end-users if the Panama-origin shipment and full payment prove real export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) - Declaración Única de Aduana de Exportación
Commercial invoice (original in Spanish or bilingual) describing HS code 8532/8533 goods
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing Panama port/airport of export
Inward remittance certificate or bank credit confirmation (SWIFT/transfer receipt) for the export proceeds
Packing list and certificate of origin (if requested)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsupported or sham zero-rating is void ab initio; the DGI claws back 7% ITBMS, plus statutory interest and surcharges of 50% to 100% of the tax for misdeclaration. Recurring fraud triggers criminal liability, suspension of RUC, and personal liability for directors under Panama's Tax Code and Customs Law. Exporter must maintain complete files for 5 to 7 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (state-owned monetary agent) in coordination with the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Panama's banking supervision authority); no autonomous central bank, US dollar is legal tender under Law 84 of 1904 and Decree Law 9 of 1998
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions; Panama operates a fully dollarized economy (no national fiat currency), so there is no legal distinction between resident and non-resident convertibility. Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject only to standard tax withholding (e.g., 10% dividend tax under territorial taxation rules) and compliance with anti-money laundering documentation for cross-border wires.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There are no statutory timeframes, no mandatory surrender requirements, and no minimum conversion ratios for export receipts because US dollars are the domestic legal tender. Exporters may retain and disburse proceeds freely in USD or any other currency without central bank reporting obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Panama's licensing framework under the Superintendency of Banks permits digital banks and fintech payment entities, but offshore digital EMIs must obtain a local authorization to offer accounts to Panamanian corporates. Offshore EMIs cannot clear through the local ACH/SWIFT infrastructure without a Panamanian banking partner. Legal constraints include the lack of a dedicated digital asset licensing regime and the requirement to maintain a physical compliance office in Panama for regulated banking activities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandated for first-time corporate clients: at least one director or the legal representative must appear before the bank's compliance officer for a face-to-face KYC interview. Remote account opening is occasionally permitted for non-resident entities, but only on a discretionary basis, subject to higher due diligence, certified document legalization, and video verification. For PA_CORP with passive electronic inventory operations, a physical board resolution authorizing signatories is strongly recommended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) shrouded through bearer shares or foundation structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled beneficial ownership declaration (Form BOD-1), sworn affidavit of identity, source of wealth report, audited financial statements, and corporate registry due diligence certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status among directors or shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file including PEP status disclosure, proof of legitimate business activity (purchase/sales contracts for MLCCs and resistors), reference letters from prior correspondent banks, and UK-based or US-based business references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction profile: low payroll but high-volume import/export invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade transaction trail: proforma invoices, bills of lading, packing lists, customs entries, warehouse receipts, and shipping insurance certificates corroborating the physical flow of Pass_Components_Inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Destination jurisdiction blacklist risk for USD clearing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYC origin of funds report, counterparty bank due diligence (not just corporate legal opinion), and letter of assurance that goods and counterparties have no embargoademarcation links, plus OFAC screening records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is SWIFT MT103/MT202 through the US correspondent network (Fedwire/CHIPS) because Panama uses the US dollar. Recommended purpose codes (ISO 20022) are 'CODT' for capital contributions, 'RECA' for trade receivables collection, or 'TREA' for trade-related advance. Verification requirements include bank account debits confirmation, corporate resolution approving the capital injection, and an SWIFT gpi tracker to ensure end-to-end traffic finality.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 (direct wire transfers) for supplier settlements and irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for large passive-component purchase orders. For intercompany transactions, MT300 (FX confirms) and MT199 (multi-bank confirmations) may be used. Supplementary rail for small-ticket disbursements is via US ACH (NACHA) only if account is domiciled with a Panama bank that participates in the US ACH gateway.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-Term Forward Contracts (non-deliverable) for CNY/EUR/JPY exposure through Panamanian banks' correspondent desks
Over-the-counter currency swaps settled in USD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies used by suppliers
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (rare but permitted with bank board approval)
Plain vanilla FX futures bought via US-regulated clearing houses

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (“Impuesto Anual de Franquicia”) — sworn payment declaration filed through the resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days following each incorporation anniversary (anniversary rule per Law 47 of 2023 and Fiscal Code Article 944)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 5% on unpaid tax until payment (capped at 50%); no tax clearance (Paz y Salvo) available; after 3 consecutive years of non-payment the DGI and Public Registry administratively dissolve and strike off the S.A.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Owner Information (Declaración Jurada Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI — Registro de Beneficiario Final (RBF), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days following each incorporation anniversary; any share transfer or change of ultimate beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Law 129 of 2020 fines from B/.100 to B/.10,000 per infringement; non-filing may trigger resident agent resignation, loss of tax clearance, and eventual administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada Anual de Renta) — required only when the S.A. derives Panamanian-source income; fully offshore passive distributors owe zero tax and may not need to file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI — Income Tax Department (Departamento de Impuestos sobre la Renta), MEF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the subsequent year for calendar-year taxpayers (within 3 months after fiscal year-end); no filing obligation for exclusively foreign-source passive income under Panama’s territorial taxation system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imposed assessment of taxes plus monthly interest/up-to-50% surcharge under Fiscal Code; denial of Paz y Salvo; penalties up to B/.10,000 for late or non-filing by the DGI

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory audit is mandatory for a private Panama S.A.; a certified public accountant (Contador Público Autorizado) report is imposed by DGI regulation when annual gross revenue exceeds B/.1,000,000; audit is also mandatory for entities supervised by the banking, securities, insurance, or other regulated sectors
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for SMV-listed and regulated entities; non-regulated S.As. may maintain books under Panama local GAAP (Código Fiscal rules) or IFRS for offshore recordkeeping; no financial statements need to be filed with the Public Registry

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent maintains the private UBO register at the registered office; each share transfer must be reflected immediately in the share register and any resulting change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be declared to the DGI’s Registro de Beneficiario Final within 30 days; the annual sworn confirmation must reconcile shareholding transfers occurring during the year and must be re-filed within 30 days after each incorporation anniversary
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Impuesto Sobre la Renta, ISR, charged on net taxable income from Panamanian-source activities; wholesale distribution of passive electronic components is within the territorial net unless the inventory is wholly held and traded abroad)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific tax holiday for ISIC 4652 distribution. Standard deductions for COGS, salaries, and operational expenditures apply. The 1.5%-of-gross-receipts monthly advance payment (pago anticipado) is creditable against the final 25% liability. NOL carryforward of 5 years is available. Export-income exemption is not available for mere resale of inventory without substantive local value-added activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 580 (Declaración Jurada de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically via the DGI SIRT / e-Tax portal (sirt.panamatramita.gob.pa); supplementary TP confirmation forms (Form 552/580-TP) may be attached.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; monthly advance payments (pagos anticipados) are declared monthly through the DGI R-1 / Form 584 module.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal-year end; calendar-year corporations must file no later than 31 March of the following year. Fiscal-year companies must file by the last day of the third month after the fiscal-year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from Panamanian-source sales of MLCC capacitors, resistors and other passive electronic inventory (ISIC 4652), plus any margin on related logistics and warehousing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not alter the S.A. entry; 100% of the S.A.'s Panamanian-source revenue must be reported regardless of parent domicile. Cross-border inventory sales that are entirely concluded, delivered and paid outside Panama may be treated as extraterritorial only when supported by commercial documentation and economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold (procured inventory value, import duties, freight allocated to the sale). Must be supported by invoices and customs declarations; related-party purchases are subject to transfer-pricing adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the purchase is made from a related foreign supplier, the TP price must be benchmarked under an approved method; otherwise, the DGI may recharacterize the transaction and disallow the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: payroll, rent, warehousing, logistics, legal/accounting, permits and financial charges allocated to the Panamanian business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees or intercompany service charges paid to non-residents are deductible only when supported by an economic-substance test and a valid TP study showing benefit to the Panamanian entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after NOL deduction (maximum 5-year carryforward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ownership has no direct effect; the S.A. computes net income as a standalone territorial taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% ISR on final net taxable income, compared with the total monthly advance payments already remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advance payments are the default mechanism; if the S.A. failed to make advances with no Panamanian activity, the DGI will apply the 1.5% monthly advance rate plus penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 / Box 130 (Saldo a Pagar o a Favor)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Remaining tax payable (or credit carryforward) after crediting advances and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund claim by the S.A. requires a solvencia fiscal (peace-and-save) certificate and a tax-audit review; refunds are rare for newly active distribution companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 2% per month or fraction of the tax due, up to 50% maximum. Late payment: monthly interest of 1.5% plus a separate fine of up to USD 5,000. The DGI will block the issuance of the solvencia fiscal certificate and may suspend the corporate registration for consecutive non-filings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends paid out of profits that were already subject to the 25% corporate tax; 10% on dividends paid from untaxed or exempt profits (e.g., extraterritorial income without substance). An additional 5% 'complementary dividend tax' arises at the corporate level on profits not distributed within 12 months of fiscal year-end.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must (1) submit an original, apostilled Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction's competent authority, (2) provide a completed DGI Form 589 (application for exemption/refund) or the specific reduced-withholding authorization request, (3) evidence beneficial ownership of the shares and absence of treaty-shopping, and (4) obtain a written DGI ruling before distribution. Without prior authorization, the payer must withhold the statutory rate; a refund may be filed later. Panama's DTA network (e.g., Mexico, South Korea, Singapore, UAE, Qatar, Portugal, Barbados) provides reduced dividend rates generally between 5% and 10%, subject to an anti-conduit clause.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest and royalties paid to non-residents is 12.5% (interest paid on external bank loans may be exempt; royalties for patents/soft IP paid to treaty residents are typically reduced to 5%-10%). Fees for technical services and leasing are generally subject to the same 12.5%-15% range. The withholding is final and must be remitted through the DGI monthly payment form (Form 581).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 2,000,000 (equivalent to PAB 2,000,000) of aggregate related-party transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory preparation and filing of the Transfer Pricing Report (Local File) and the related-party disclosure annex (Form 552/580-TP). Transactions below the threshold require only an intercompany policy statement and arm's-length justification in the tax file.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Profit Split Method (for joint value chains)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Requirements (ESR; territorial-reform legislation, including Ley 254 de 2021 and the DGI substance regulations) apply to a PA_CORP S.A. deriving income from 'relevant activities' such as distribution, service-centre operations, and logistics. A passive electronic-components distributor must maintain in Panama: (i) a physical office or storage facility, (ii) adequate full-time employees making distribution and inventory decisions, (iii) local bank accounts and books, and (iv) an annual substance report filed with the DGI. Failure to meet ESR exposes the company to characterization as a shell and to the re-attribution of income to the non-resident principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or using false invoices (facturas falsas) to inflate COGS, under-declaring gross sales on Form 580, or deliberately failing to make monthly advance payments while conducting actual physical deliveries in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax-fraud penalties under Panama's Penal Tax Regime: imprisonment of 3 to 6 years and a fine of up to 10 times the evaded tax; DGI also imposes the 2% monthly surcharge, terminates fiscal solvency, and publishes the taxpayer in the public delinquency register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and face civil restitution orders; the DGI may obtain travel bans on directors and legal representatives until the debt is secured.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a shell: no physical premises or employees in Panama, all inventory and cash managed abroad, no locally maintained accounting records, and the registered agent being the only point of contact, while the S.A. invoices Panamanian clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to USD 10,000 under the ESR/dissolution procedures; the DGI may disregard the entity and confiscate its tax benefits, and the Public Registry may dissolve the company for failing to maintain a resident agent or file accounting records. The company loses its territorial tax defence, and all income is re-characterized as Panamanian-source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under the alter-ego doctrine, making the directors personally liable for unpaid corporate tax and third-party debts; directors may also be prohibited from incorporating new Panamanian companies for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PA_CORP S.A. as an undisclosed pass-through for third-party fund transfers related to the electronic inventory trade, failing to register the final beneficial owner in the Panamanian registry, or omitting the substance declaration in respect of cross-border related-party flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML Law 23 of 2015 and the Beneficial Owner Law: administrative fines up to USD 1,000,000 per violation, criminal sanctions for predicate money-laundering offences (imprisonment up to 12 years), and revocation of the resident agent's licence. The DGI may also impose a 30% withholding assessment on unrevealed shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil restitution of laundered amounts, confiscation of personal assets, travel bans, and imprisonment if they knowingly executed the transactions; compliance officers and registered agents are subject to the same enforcement.
